definition_en: to discover something by searching, to come upon something, to consider something to be a certain way, or to make a legal decision
core_image: 手伸进沙发缝里，摸到那串丢失的钥匙
scene: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
sceneCN: 这里 find 是「找到」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。

senses.title: To locate by searching
senses.definition: to discover something you have been looking for
senses.definitionCN: 找到一直在寻找的东西
senses.example: She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of searching.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常生活中搜寻的义项。

senses.title: To come upon
senses.definition: to discover something without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 无意中遇到或发现某物
senses.example: We found a small café near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近发现了一家小咖啡馆。
senses.why: Some things are found by chance.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西是偶然发现的。

senses.title: To consider
senses.definition: to feel or think that something is a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 觉得或认为某事是某种样子
senses.example: I find this book very useful.
senses.exampleCN: 我觉得这本书很有用。
senses.why: Experience shapes our judgment.
senses.whyCN: 经历会影响我们的判断。

senses.title: To decide a case
senses.definition: to make a legal decision about a case
senses.definitionCN: 对案件作出法律裁定
senses.example: The jury found him innocent.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团裁定他无罪。
senses.why: A court also reaches a finding.
senses.whyCN: 法庭也会给出裁断。

intro.en: Find comes from Old English findan, to come upon, and has kept that core meaning for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: find 源自古英语 findan（遇到、发现），一千多年来一直保留着这个核心含义。

items.en: Findan meant to come upon something.
items.cn: findan 意为遇到某物。

items.en: The verb also covered opinion and judgment.
items.cn: 这个动词也包含看法与判断。

items.en: Found became the past tense.
items.cn: found 成为过去式。

items.en: Find out extended the idea of discovery.
items.cn: find out 扩展了发现的含义。

items.en: Legal use named the verdict of a court.
items.cn: 法律用法指法庭的裁断。

note.en: Find is compared with similar-looking words and with words for discovery.
note.cn: 把 find 与形近词以及表示发现的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sum of money set aside
to learn or notice for the first time
to find the exact place of

normalIntro.en: Find is the plain verb for coming upon something, whether by search or by chance.
normalIntro.cn: find 是表示遇到某物的基本动词，无论靠寻找还是靠偶然。

normal.en: You find what you look for.
normal.cn: 你寻找的东西会被你找到。

normal.en: We found a café by chance.
normal.cn: 我们偶然发现了一家咖啡馆。

normal.en: Find out means to learn a fact.
normal.cn: find out 意为查明一个事实。

normal.en: A jury can find a person innocent.
normal.cn: 陪审团可以裁定一个人无罪。

normal.en: The past tense of find is found.

abstract.en: To find is to close the distance between wanting and having.
abstract.cn: 找到，就是缩短渴望与拥有之间的距离。

abstract.en: Some discoveries arrive without a search.
abstract.cn: 有些发现并不需要寻找。

abstract.en: What we find often changes what we were looking for.
abstract.cn: 我们找到的东西，常常改变我们原本寻找的东西。

examples.en: She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
examples.cn: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。

examples.en: We found a small café near the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站附近发现了一家小咖啡馆。

examples.en: I find this book very useful.
examples.cn: 我觉得这本书很有用。

dict_mnemonic.text: find 源自古英语 findan（遇到），不规则变化为 find、found、found。

root: 源自古英语 findan（遇到、发现），核心义「遇见并得到」。

sensesIntro.en: Find means to locate, to come upon, to consider, or to give a legal decision.
sensesIntro.cn: find 意为找到、发现、认为或作出裁决。

core.en: To come upon something or someone.
core.cn: 遇到某物或某人。

branches.en: To locate after searching.
To meet something by chance.
To form an opinion.
To reach a legal verdict.
Chance and judgment both begin with meeting.
branches.cn: 偶然与判断都始于遇见。

intro.en: Find is a native Germanic verb with a strong and irregular past tense.
intro.cn: find 是日耳曼语本族动词，过去式强变化且不规则。

latinIntro.en: Find has no Latin ancestor; Latin invenire, to come upon, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: find 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 invenire（遇到）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She finds new ideas every day.
items.exampleCN: 她每天都能发现新想法。

items.meaningCN: 找到（过去式与过去分词）

items.exampleCN: 找到答案花了几个小时。

items.example: The findings were published last week.

items.exampleCN: 他带着新获得的自信说话。

items.example: The file is findable by name.
items.exampleCN: 这个文件可以按名称找到。

definition_zh: 好的；精美的；晴朗的；细小的；罚款
definition_en: of high quality, delicate or carefully made, bright and clear, very small, or a sum of money paid as a penalty
core_image: 雨后天空干净透亮，远山的轮廓都看得很清楚
scene: 今天天气很好，正适合散步。The weather is fine today, perfect for a walk.
sceneCN: 这里 fine 是「晴朗的」（第 3 个义项）；句意：今天天气很好，正适合散步。

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: very good or of high quality
senses.definitionCN: 很好或质量很高的
senses.example: She is a fine musician.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位出色的音乐家。
senses.why: The core sense praises quality.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是对品质的称赞。

senses.title: Delicately made
senses.definition: delicate, thin, or carefully made
senses.definitionCN: 精致、纤细或做工讲究的
senses.example: The dress has fine lace.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子有精美的蕾丝。
senses.why: Fine work is work done with care.
senses.whyCN: 精细的活计是用心做出来的。

senses.title: Bright and clear
senses.definition: sunny and clear, without rain
senses.definitionCN: 阳光充足、晴朗无雨的
senses.example: The weather is fine today, perfect for a walk.
senses.exampleCN: 今天天气很好，正适合散步。
senses.why: Clear weather is also called fine.
senses.whyCN: 晴朗的天气也称作 fine。

senses.title: Very small
senses.definition: very thin or made of tiny particles
senses.definitionCN: 极细的或由微小颗粒组成的
senses.example: Fine dust covered the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 细小的灰尘落满了架子。
senses.why: Thin strands and grains are fine.
senses.whyCN: 细丝与细颗粒都可用 fine。

senses.title: Money penalty
senses.definition: a sum of money paid as a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 作为惩罚支付的一笔钱
senses.example: He had to pay a parking fine.
senses.exampleCN: 他不得不缴纳违章停车罚款。
senses.why: The noun names the payment that ends a case.
senses.whyCN: 名词指了结案件的这笔付款。

intro.en: Fine comes from Latin finis, an end, and first meant finished or perfected.
intro.cn: fine 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），最初意为「完成的、完善的」。

items.en: Finis meant an end or a limit.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或界限。

items.en: Fin meant finished or perfected.
items.cn: fin 意为完成的或完善的。

items.en: Fine came to mean of high quality.
items.cn: fine 逐渐指品质优良。

items.en: The word extended to clear weather and thin particles.
items.cn: 这个词又扩展到晴朗天气与细小颗粒。

items.en: The noun named a money penalty.
items.cn: 名词形式指金钱处罚。

note.en: Fine is compared with similar-looking words and with words for quality and penalties.
note.cn: 把 fine 与形近词以及表示品质和处罚的词作比较。

entries.definition: a punishment for breaking a rule

normalIntro.en: Fine stretches from perfect quality to thin particles and even to a sum of money.
normalIntro.cn: fine 从完美的品质一路延伸到细小颗粒，甚至一笔罚金。

normal.en: Fine weather is clear and sunny.
normal.cn: fine weather 指晴朗的天气。

normal.en: Fine lace is delicate and beautiful.
normal.cn: 精细的蕾丝既纤巧又美丽。

normal.en: Fine dust floats in the air.
normal.cn: 细小的灰尘飘浮在空气中。

normal.en: A fine is money paid for a rule broken.
normal.cn: 罚款是因违规而支付的钱。

normal.en: The finest work takes the most care.
normal.cn: 最精细的作品需要最用心。

abstract.en: To finish something is to make it fine.
abstract.cn: 把一件事做完，就是把它做精。

abstract.en: What is fine can be either perfect or merely thin.
abstract.cn: fine 既可以是完美，也可以只是纤细。

abstract.en: A line between good and bad is often a fine one.
abstract.cn: 好坏之间的界线往往只有一线之差。

examples.en: The weather is fine today, perfect for a walk.
examples.cn: 今天天气很好，正适合散步。

examples.en: She is a fine musician.
examples.cn: 她是一位出色的音乐家。

examples.en: Fine dust covered the shelf.
examples.cn: 细小的灰尘落满了架子。

dict_mnemonic.text: fine 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），本义「完成的、完善的」，后引申出晴朗、纤细与罚款。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束、界限），核心义「到了尽头的圆满」。

sensesIntro.en: Fine means excellent, delicate, clear, very small, or a money penalty.
sensesIntro.cn: fine 意为优良的、精美的、晴朗的、细小的或罚款。

core.en: Something brought to its finished, perfect state.
core.cn: 被带到完成、圆满状态的事物。

branches.en: Finished means excellent.
Careful work makes delicate things.
branches.cn: 用心之作造就精致之物。

branches.en: Clear skies feel perfect.
branches.cn: 晴朗天空让人感到完美。

branches.en: Tiny grains are the finest form.
branches.cn: 微小颗粒是最细的形态。

branches.en: A payment ends a legal case.
branches.cn: 一笔付款了结一桩案件。

intro.en: Fine is a short Latin-derived word that grows many relatives through prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: fine 源自拉丁语，词形简短，通过前缀和后缀衍生出许多同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root finis, an end, links fine with finish, final, and finance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 finis（结束）把 fine 与 finish、final、finance 联系起来。

items.example: This thread is finer than that one.
The fineness of the powder matters.
The oil refinery runs day and night.

latinEntries.example: Finis gave fine its sense of completion.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finis 赋予 fine「完成」的含义。

latinEntries.example: Finire led to the English word finish.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finire 演变为英语单词 finish。

definition_zh: 手指；指状物；用手指触碰
definition_en: one of the long parts of the hand, a part shaped like a finger, or to touch something with the fingers
core_image: 指尖落在琴键上，轻轻按下一个音
scene: 他用手指点了点地图上的位置。He pointed a finger at the spot on the map.
sceneCN: 这里 finger 是「手指」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用手指点了点地图上的位置。

senses.title: Part of the hand
senses.definition: one of the long thin parts at the end of the hand
senses.definitionCN: 手末端细长的部位之一
senses.example: He pointed a finger at the spot on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 他用手指点了点地图上的位置。
senses.why: This is the basic body-part sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的身体部位义项。

senses.title: Finger-shaped part
senses.definition: something long and narrow that looks like a finger
senses.definitionCN: 细长、形似手指的东西
senses.example: A finger of light came through the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 一道指状的光从窗帘缝里透进来。
senses.why: Shape names many objects by analogy.
senses.whyCN: 人们常用形状来类比命名物体。

senses.title: To touch with fingers
senses.definition: to touch or handle something with the fingers
senses.definitionCN: 用手指触摸或摆弄某物
senses.example: He fingered the coin in his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他在口袋里用手指摩挲那枚硬币。
senses.why: The body part becomes a verb of touch.
senses.whyCN: 身体部位转化为触摸的动作。

intro.en: Finger is an old Germanic word, recorded in Old English as finger, with the same meaning it has today.
intro.cn: finger 是古老的日耳曼词，古英语中写作 finger，含义与今天相同。

items.en: Fingraz named a finger of the hand.
items.cn: fingraz 指手上的手指。

items.en: Finger kept the same meaning.
items.cn: finger 保留了相同的含义。

items.en: Fingers named finger-shaped parts.
items.cn: fingers 开始指形似手指的部件。

items.en: The verb meant to touch with the fingers.
items.cn: 动词形式意为用手指触碰。

items.en: Compounds such as fingertip appeared.
items.cn: fingertip 等复合词出现。

note.en: Finger is compared with similar-looking words and with words for hand parts.
note.cn: 把 finger 与形近词以及表示手部部位的词作比较。

entries.definition: the short thick digit of the hand

normalIntro.en: Finger names the long parts of the hand and also anything shaped like one.
normalIntro.cn: finger 指手上细长的部位，也指任何形似手指的东西。

normal.en: The index finger points the way.
She crossed her fingers for luck.
A finger of light entered the room.
normal.cn: 一道指状的光射进房间。

normal.en: Finger food is eaten by hand.
Fingertip is the end of a finger.

abstract.en: A finger can point, hold, feel, and speak.
abstract.cn: 一根手指能指、能握、能感觉，也能表达。

abstract.en: The smallest part of the hand can do the finest work.
abstract.cn: 手上最小的部分，能完成最精细的工作。

abstract.en: To point a finger is also to place blame.
abstract.cn: 伸出手指，有时也是把责任指向别人。

examples.en: He pointed a finger at the spot on the map.
examples.cn: 他用手指点了点地图上的位置。

examples.en: A finger of light came through the curtain.
examples.cn: 一道指状的光从窗帘缝里透进来。

examples.en: He fingered the coin in his pocket.
examples.cn: 他在口袋里用手指摩挲那枚硬币。

dict_mnemonic.text: finger 是日耳曼语本族词，核心义「手指」，也可指形似手指的细长物。

root: 源自古英语 finger（手指），与德语 Finger 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Finger means a part of the hand, a finger-shaped thing, or to touch with the fingers.
sensesIntro.cn: finger 意为手指、指状物或用手指触碰。

core.en: A long, narrow part of the hand used to touch and point.
core.cn: 手上用于触碰和指示的细长部位。

branches.en: The body part itself.
Anything shaped like a finger.
The action of touching.
The part and its action share a form.
branches.cn: 部位与动作共用一个形式。

branches.en: Shape links the hand to the world.
branches.cn: 形状把手指与世界联系起来。

intro.en: Finger is a native Germanic word that forms many compounds.
intro.cn: finger 是日耳曼语本族词，能构成许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: Finger has no Latin ancestor; Latin digitus, a finger, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: finger 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 digitus（手指）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 她用手指摸了摸柔软的布。

items.example: The fingering of the strings was light.
The answer is at your fingertips.

items.exampleCN: 这种植物有指状的叶子。

definition_zh: 完成；结束；终点；表面处理
definition_en: to complete something, to come to an end, the end of something, or a surface treatment
core_image: 笔尖在最后一题上停住，试卷被轻轻合上
scene: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。She finished the last question and put down her pen.
sceneCN: 这里 finish 是「完成」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她答完最后一题，放下了笔。

senses.title: To complete
senses.definition: to bring a task or activity to its end
senses.definitionCN: 把任务或活动做到结尾
senses.example: She finished the last question and put down her pen.
senses.exampleCN: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。
senses.why: This is the most common everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的日常义项。

senses.title: To come to an end
senses.definition: to stop or end, especially at a planned time
senses.definitionCN: 停止或结束，尤指在预定时间结束
senses.example: The meeting finished at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议在中午结束。
senses.why: Events as well as tasks can finish.
senses.whyCN: 不只是任务，事件也会结束。

senses.title: The end of a race
senses.definition: the last part or end of something, such as a race
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的最后部分或终点，如比赛的终点
senses.example: The race had a close finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这场比赛的最后阶段竞争激烈。
senses.why: The noun names the ending point.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指结束的那个点。

senses.title: Surface treatment
senses.definition: the way a surface is treated or coated
senses.definitionCN: 表层的处理方式或涂层
senses.example: The table has a smooth finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子表面很光滑。
senses.why: A finished surface is the last stage of making.
senses.whyCN: 表面处理是制作过程的最后一步。

intro.en: Finish comes from Latin finis, an end, through Old French finir, to bring to an end.
intro.cn: finish 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经古法语 finir（使结束）传入英语。

items.en: Finis meant an end or boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界。

items.en: Finir meant to bring to an end.
items.cn: finir 意为使某事结束。

items.en: Finishen meant to complete.
items.cn: finishen 意为完成。

items.en: Finish named the end of a race.
items.cn: finish 指比赛的终点。

items.en: Finish also named a surface treatment.
items.cn: finish 又指表面处理。

note.en: Finish is compared with similar-looking words and with words for completing.
note.cn: 把 finish 与形近词以及表示完成的词作比较。

entries.definition: to bring something to a close

normalIntro.en: Finish moves from doing the last step to naming the last point.
normalIntro.cn: finish 从做最后一步，延伸到命名最后那个点。

normal.en: Finish your homework before dinner.
The film finishes at nine.
The finish line is close.
A smooth finish makes wood shine.
normal.cn: 光滑的表面处理让木头发亮。

normal.en: Add a finishing touch to the cake.
normal.cn: 给蛋糕加上最后的点缀。

abstract.en: Every ending is also a boundary drawn in time.
abstract.cn: 每一个结束，也是在时间里画下的一道边界。

abstract.en: To finish is to decide that enough has been done.
abstract.cn: 完成，就是决定已经做得足够。

abstract.en: The last touch often reveals the whole craft.
abstract.cn: 最后一步，往往显露整门手艺。

examples.en: She finished the last question and put down her pen.
examples.cn: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。

examples.en: The meeting finished at noon.
examples.cn: 会议在中午结束。

examples.en: The table has a smooth finish.
examples.cn: 这张桌子表面很光滑。

dict_mnemonic.text: finish 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经古法语 finir 进入英语，核心义「做到尽头」。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束、界限），核心义「到达尽头」。

sensesIntro.en: Finish means to complete, to end, the end point, or a surface treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: finish 意为完成、结束、终点或表面处理。

core.en: Reaching the end of a task or object.
core.cn: 到达任务或物体的尽头。

branches.en: Doing the last step of a task.
An event reaching its end.
The final point itself.
The final treatment of a surface.
The action and the place share one word.
branches.cn: 动作与位置共用一个词。

intro.en: Finish grows from the Latin root finis through French and English suffixes.
intro.cn: finish 从拉丁词根 finis 出发，经由法语和英语后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: The Latin finis and finire also gave final, finance, and define.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 与 finire 也孕育了 final、finance 和 define。

items.example: I will finish the report tonight.
An unfinished painting stood on the easel.
items.exampleCN: 画架上放着一幅未完成的画。
他们给旧地板重新做了表面处理。

definition_en: flames that burn, a destructive burning, a stove or fireplace, the shooting of guns, or to dismiss someone from a job
core_image: 黑夜里的火堆噼啪作响，橘红的火舌向上卷
scene: 孩子们围坐在火堆旁取暖。The children sat around the fire to keep warm.
sceneCN: 这里 fire 是「火」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们围坐在火堆旁取暖。

senses.title: Burning flames
senses.definition: the heat and light produced by burning

senses.title: To introduce the first point in a list
senses.titleCN: 第一；首先（列举中的第一点）
senses.definition: used to begin the first item when you are going to mention several items one by one
senses.definitionCN: 当你准备逐条列出若干要点时，用来引出第一条
senses.example: Firstly, I would like to thank everyone who helped with the project.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，我要感谢所有为这个项目提供帮助的人。
senses.why: The word is first plus the adverb ending -ly, so it literally means doing something in the first place.
senses.whyCN: firstly 由 first（第一）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面意思就是「处在第一位地」，于是专门用于开启列举。

senses.title: To signal order before other points follow
senses.titleCN: 提示顺序；预告还有下文
senses.definition: used to tell the listener that more points are coming after this one
senses.definitionCN: 用来告诉听者：这条之后还有更多要点，请按顺序听
senses.example: There are two reasons why I disagree. Firstly, the data is outdated.
senses.exampleCN: 我不同意有两个原因。第一，数据已经过时了。
senses.why: Because firstly only marks position one, its very use promises a secondly or thirdly to come.
senses.whyCN: firstly 只标记「第一位」，所以它一出现就暗示后面会有「第二」「第三」，起到预告顺序的作用。

senses.title: To open a formal argument or explanation
senses.definition: used in formal speech or writing to organize an argument in clear steps
senses.definitionCN: 在正式口头或书面表达中，用来把论述分成清晰的步骤
senses.example: The report firstly examines the causes of the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告首先考察了危机的成因。
senses.why: Formal writing favors explicit ordering words, and firstly makes the first step visible to the reader.
senses.whyCN: 正式文体偏爱显性的顺序标记，firstly 把「第一步」明确摆在读者面前，使论述结构一目了然。

senses.title: To rank the most important reason first
senses.titleCN: 把最重要的理由放在第一
senses.definition: used to put the weightiest point at the head of a list for emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 把最关键的一点放在列表最前面，以示强调
senses.example: Firstly and above all, safety must come before speed.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，也是最重要的：安全必须排在速度之前。
senses.why: Putting a point in first position naturally marks it as primary, so firstly can carry emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 被放在「第一位」的要点天然带有首要性，因此 firstly 也可以承载强调功能。

senses.title: To replace first in enumerated speech
senses.titleCN: 替代 first 作列举副词
senses.definition: used instead of first when first might be read as an adjective or noun
senses.definitionCN: 在 first 可能被误读为形容词或名词时，用它明确副词身份
senses.example: Firstly, check the power supply before touching the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 第一，先检查电源，然后再碰机器。
senses.why: The -ly ending makes the adverbial role unambiguous, which is why some writers prefer it.
senses.whyCN: -ly 后缀让副词身份毫无歧义，这正是部分作者在列举时更愿意用 firstly 的原因。

senses.title: To open a summary or recap
senses.definition: used to begin restating previously made points in order
senses.definitionCN: 在结尾按顺序复述先前要点时作开头用
senses.example: To conclude, firstly we agreed on the budget, and then on the timeline.
senses.exampleCN: 总结一下：第一，我们敲定了预算；然后敲定了时间表。
senses.why: Recaps reuse the original order of the list, so the first restated point is again marked firstly.
senses.whyCN: 复述沿用原本的列举顺序，被放在第一位的要点再次用 firstly 标记。

senses.title: To structure spoken instructions
senses.definition: used when giving step-by-step spoken directions or procedures
senses.definitionCN: 口头给出一步步的操作指引或流程时使用
senses.example: Firstly, open the lid, then pour in the rice.
senses.exampleCN: 第一步，先打开锅盖，然后倒入大米。
senses.why: Procedures are lists of actions, and the first action naturally gets the first marker.
senses.whyCN: 操作流程就是动作清单，第一个动作自然配上「第一」这个标记。

senses.title: To mark the first of paired contrasts
senses.titleCN: 标记成对对照中的前者
senses.definition: used to present the first side of a two-part comparison or contrast
senses.definitionCN: 用于呈现两部分对比中的前一部分
senses.example: The plan has strengths and weaknesses. Firstly, it is cheap to run.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划有利有弊。第一，它运营成本低。
senses.why: Contrast also works as an ordered list, so the first item still receives firstly.
senses.whyCN: 对比本质上也是一种有顺序的列举，前一项同样由 firstly 来标记。

intro.en: Firstly is a transparent English formation: the adverb ending -ly added to first, an old Germanic ordinal.
intro.cn: firstly 是一个构成透明的英语词：在古老的日耳曼语序数词 first 后面加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: The root behind first is generally reconstructed as *per-, *pre- meaning forward or before, seen in related forms across many Indo-European languages.
items.cn: 一般认为 first 的词根可重构为 *per-、*pre-，意为「向前；在前」，在多个印欧语的同源词中可见。

items.en: The comparative form *frumizon and related superlative forms developed in Germanic, giving Old English forms such as fyrmest and fyrst, meaning earliest or foremost.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中发展出比较级形式 *frumizon 及相关最高级形式，古英语由此产生 fyrmest、fyrst 等词形，义为「最早的；最前的」。

items.en: By the ninth century, fyrst was established as the superlative of fore, meaning before, so first literally means most before, that is, earliest.
items.cn: 到九世纪，fyrst 已确立为 fore（在前）的最高级，所以 first 的字面义是「最在前」，即「最早」。

items.en: Firstly is first recorded in the sixteenth century; earlier English writers typically used first alone as the list-opening adverb.
items.cn: firstly 最早见于十六世纪的记载；更早的英语作者通常只用 first 兼作列举副词。

items.en: Since the eighteenth century, usage commentators have debated whether firstly is necessary, since first does the same job; both remain in common formal use today.
items.cn: 自十八世纪以来，用法评论者一直争论 firstly 是否必要，因为 first 也能承担同样功能；如今两者在正式语体中都很常用。

items.en: Firstly is common in British formal writing, while American style guides often prefer first; the choice is stylistic rather than grammatical.
items.cn: firstly 在英式正式书面语中常见，而美式风格指南多偏好 first；这种选择属于文体偏好，而非语法问题。

note.en: Watch out for the near-identical first, which can do the same job, and for other ordering adverbs that continue the list.
note.cn: 注意与它几乎同义的 first（同样可用于列举开头），以及继续往下列举的其他顺序副词。

entries.definition: ordinal number and adverb meaning before all others; can replace firstly in lists
entries.definitionCN: 序数词兼副词，义为「第一；最先」，在列举中可替代 firstly

entries.definition: adjective or noun for the child born earliest in a family
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，指家中最早出生的孩子，与 firstly 共享 first 词根

entries.definition: adverb meaning in a firm or steady way; spelled similarly but from firm, not first
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「坚定地；牢固地」，拼写与 firstly 相近，但词根是 firm 而非 first

entries.definition: adverb introducing the second point in a list, usually after firstly or first
entries.definitionCN: 引出列举中第二点的副词，通常紧跟 firstly 或 first 之后

entries.definition: adverb meaning at the beginning, often describing a starting state rather than a list position
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「起初；开始时」，多描述起始状态而非列举位置

entries.definition: phrase used to open the first point, more conversational than firstly
entries.definitionCN: 用于引出第一点的短语，比 firstly 更口语化

normalIntro.en: Five down-to-earth ways to lock firstly into memory using its real building blocks.
normalIntro.cn: 五个基于真实构词的接地气方法，帮你把 firstly 记牢。

normal.en: Split it: first + ly, meaning in the first way or in first place.
normal.cn: 拆开记：first + ly，即「以第一的方式；在第一位」。

normal.en: Pair it with secondly: wherever firstly appears, a secondly is waiting in line.
normal.cn: 与 secondly 配对记：firstly 一出现，secondly 就在后面排队。

normal.en: Recall first means most before, so firstly means speaking from the most-before position.
normal.cn: 联想 first 的本义「最在前」，firstly 就是「从最前面的位置说起」。

normal.en: Practice the set: firstly, secondly, thirdly — a counting chant for arguments.
normal.cn: 练三连：firstly、secondly、thirdly——给论点报数的小口诀。

normal.en: Contrast with initially: initially means at the start of time, firstly means at the head of a list.
normal.cn: 与 initially 对比记：initially 指「时间上的起初」，firstly 指「列表中的第一

abstract.en: Picture a queue of arguments at a ticket window; the one holding ticket number one shouts firstly.
abstract.cn: 想象一排论点在售票窗口排队，手里拿一号票的那个喊出 firstly。

abstract.en: See an index finger pointing at line one of your notes, tapping twice: that tap is firstly.
abstract.cn: 想象食指指着笔记第一行敲两下：那两下敲击就是 firstly。

abstract.en: Feel a relay race where the first runner must hand off the baton; her start signal is firstly.
abstract.cn: 想象接力赛第一棒必须交出接力棒，她的起跑信号就是 firstly。

examples.en: Firstly, let me outline the three problems we identified.
examples.cn: 首先，让我概述我们发现的三个问题。

examples.en: The essay firstly introduces the theory, then applies it to real cases.
examples.cn: 文章首先介绍理论，然后将其应用于真实案例。

examples.en: She opened the meeting with a short greeting.
examples.cn: 她以简短的问候开始了会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛斯得利」——佛祖先「斯」得「利」：佛祖也讲究先来后到，第一份好处归排在第一位的人，所以 firstly 就是「第一；首先」。

root: firstly 由古英语序数词 first（源自 fore「在前」的最高级 fyrst，义为「最早；最前」）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面义为「以第一的位置」。词根可追溯至原始印欧语的 *per-、*pre-（向前；在前），属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: From its transparent build, first plus -ly, firstly spreads from marking the first list item into ordering, emphasis, and structured speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 从 first 加 -ly 的透明构造出发，firstly 由「标记列表第一项」扩展到顺序提示、强调功能和结构化表达。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing at the head of a queue of points, holding ticket number one
core.cn: 核心意象：站在一排论点的队首，手里攥着一号票

branches.en: introducing the first item and clarifying its adverb role
branches.cn: 引出第一项并明确其副词身份

branches.en: promising more points to come and structuring contrasts
branches.cn: 预告后文并组织对比结构

branches.en: organizing formal arguments and spoken procedures
branches.cn: 组织正式论述与口头流程

branches.en: ranking the weightiest reason in first place
branches.cn: 把最重要的理由排在首位

branches.en: reopening a summary in the original order
branches.cn: 按原顺序开启总结复述

intro.en: Firstly is built from the ordinal first plus the adverbial suffix -ly; related words show how first branches into a family.
intro.cn: firstly 由序数词 first 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；相关词展示出 first 如何派生出一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Firstly itself is Germanic in origin, but Latin cousins that express before and first show the shared Indo-European idea.
latinIntro.cn: firstly 本身源自日耳曼语，但拉丁语中表达「在前；第一」的同族词体现了共同的印欧观念。

items.example: firstly = first + ly, in the first place
items.exampleCN: firstly 即 first 加 ly，义为「在第一位地」

items.example: the first step is the hardest

items.exampleCN: 预见、预言中的 fore- 即此前缀
prepare、predict 中的 pre- 与 first 同源于「在前」的观念

definition_en: an animal that lives in water, the flesh of this animal eaten as food, or to try to catch fish
core_image: 湖面上鱼线轻轻一沉，水面荡开一圈涟漪
scene: 我们整个下午都在湖边钓鱼。We fished at the lake all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 fish 是「钓鱼」（第 3 个义项）；句意：我们整个下午都在湖边钓鱼。

senses.title: Water animal
senses.definition: an animal that lives in water and has fins
senses.definitionCN: 生活在水里、有鳍的动物
senses.example: The pond is full of fish.

senses.why: This is the basic animal sense.

senses.title: Food from fish
senses.definition: the flesh of a fish eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物食用的鱼肉
senses.example: We had fish for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚饭吃了鱼。
senses.why: The animal also names the meal.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物也成了餐桌上的食物名。

senses.title: To catch fish
senses.definition: to try to catch fish
senses.definitionCN: 尝试捕捉鱼类
senses.example: We fished at the lake all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整个下午都在湖边钓鱼。
senses.why: The noun becomes the activity.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为这项活动。

intro.en: Fish is an old Germanic word, from Proto-Germanic fiskaz and Old English fisc.
intro.cn: fish 是古老的日耳曼词，来自原始日耳曼语 fiskaz 和古英语 fisc。

items.en: Fiskaz named a fish.
items.cn: fiskaz 指鱼。

items.en: Fisc meant fish or fish food.
items.cn: fisc 意为鱼或鱼肉。

items.en: Fish kept both animal and food senses.
items.cn: fish 同时保留动物与食物两个义项。

items.en: The verb meant to catch fish.
items.cn: 动词形式意为捕鱼。

items.en: Fish formed many compounds.
items.cn: fish 构成了许多复合词。

note.en: Fish is compared with similar-looking words and with words for catching and eating fish.
note.cn: 把 fish 与形近词以及表示捕鱼和食鱼的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fish is the animal, the food on the plate, and the quiet afternoon by the water.
normalIntro.cn: fish 是水里的动物、盘中的食物，也是水边安静的午后。

normal.en: Fish swim in the clear water.
We ate fish and rice.
He goes fishing every Sunday.
normal.cn: 他每个星期天都去钓鱼。

normal.en: The fish market opens early.
Fish and chips is a British dish.
normal.cn: 炸鱼薯条是一道英国菜。

abstract.en: Water hides a whole world we can only visit with lines and nets.
abstract.cn: 水藏着一个世界，我们只能靠线和网去拜访。

abstract.en: Waiting for a fish teaches patience.
abstract.cn: 等鱼上钩，教会人耐心。

abstract.en: The same word feeds the body and describes the hunt.
abstract.cn: 同一个词，既喂养身体，也描述捕猎。

examples.en: We fished at the lake all afternoon.
examples.cn: 我们整个下午都在湖边钓鱼。

examples.en: We had fish for dinner.
examples.cn: 我们晚饭吃了鱼。

dict_mnemonic.text: fish 是日耳曼语本族词，既是「鱼」，也是「鱼肉」，还能作动词「钓鱼」。

root: 源自古英语 fisc（鱼），与德语 Fisch 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Fish means a water animal, its flesh as food, or the act of catching it.

core.en: A creature of water that people catch and eat.

branches.en: The living animal.

intro.en: Fish is a native Germanic word with many compound relatives.
intro.cn: fish 是日耳曼语本族词，有许多复合词亲属。

definition_zh: 合适的；健康的；合身；适合；安装
definition_en: suitable for a purpose, healthy and strong, to be the right size, to be suitable for something, or to install something
core_image: 鞋带系紧，脚在鞋里恰好贴合
scene: 这双鞋很合脚。This pair of shoes fits well.
sceneCN: 这里 fit 是「合身」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这双鞋很合脚。

senses.title: Suitable
senses.definition: suitable or right for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 适合某个用途的、恰当的
senses.example: This film is fit for children.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影适合儿童观看。
senses.why: Suitability is the broadest sense.
senses.whyCN: 适合性是最宽泛的义项。

senses.title: Healthy
senses.definition: healthy and strong, especially through exercise
senses.definitionCN: 健康强壮的，尤指通过锻炼
senses.example: She runs to keep fit.
senses.exampleCN: 她跑步以保持健康。
senses.why: A body in good shape is fit.
senses.whyCN: 状态良好的身体就是 fit。

senses.title: Right size
senses.definition: to be the right size or shape for someone
senses.definitionCN: 尺寸或形状正好适合某人
senses.example: This pair of shoes fits well.
senses.exampleCN: 这双鞋很合脚。
senses.why: Clothing is the everyday testing ground.
senses.whyCN: 衣服是这个词最常见的测试场。

senses.title: To suit
senses.definition: to be suitable for something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 适合某事或某人
senses.example: The job fits her skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作适合她的技能。
senses.why: What matches a need fits it.
senses.whyCN: 与需求相匹配，就是适合。

senses.title: To install
senses.definition: to put a part or device into place
senses.definitionCN: 把部件或装置放到正确位置
senses.example: They fitted a new lock.
senses.exampleCN: 他们装了一把新锁。
senses.why: A part that fits is placed in place.
senses.whyCN: 能贴合的部分被安置到位。

intro.en: Fit appeared in late Middle English with the sense of matching or being suited; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: fit 出现在中古英语晚期，意为「相配、适合」，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Fit meant a match or a contest.
items.cn: fit 指匹配或较量。

items.en: Fit came to mean suited or proper.
items.cn: fit 引申为适合的、恰当的。

items.en: Fit described clothing that matches the body.
items.cn: fit 描述衣服与身体相合。

items.en: Fit meant healthy and in good condition.
items.cn: fit 意为健康、状态良好。

items.en: The verb named the placing of a part.
items.cn: 动词形式指把部件安装到位。

note.en: Fit is compared with similar-looking words and with words for suitability and health.
note.cn: 把 fit 与形近词以及表示适合和健康的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fit links a good match: clothes that match the body, work that matches skills, a part that matches its place.
normalIntro.cn: fit 连接着各种「相配」：衣服配身体、工作配技能、零件配位置。

normal.en: These shoes fit perfectly.
Exercise keeps you fit.
The key fits the lock.
He fits in well at school.
They fitted new windows.

abstract.en: To fit is to find the place where something belongs.
abstract.cn: 适合，就是找到某物所属的位置。

abstract.en: A healthy body and a proper word share the same name.
abstract.cn: 健康的身体与恰当的词，共用一个名字。

abstract.en: What fits does not need force.
abstract.cn: 真正合适的东西，不需要硬塞。

examples.en: This pair of shoes fits well.
examples.cn: 这双鞋很合脚。

examples.en: She runs to keep fit.
examples.cn: 她跑步以保持健康。

examples.en: They fitted a new lock.
examples.cn: 他们装了一把新锁。

dict_mnemonic.text: fit 是中古英语晚期出现的词，核心义「相配、合适」，后引申出健康与安装。

root: 源自中古英语 fit（相配、较量），更深来源不确定，核心义「恰好相合」。

sensesIntro.en: Fit means suitable, healthy, right in size, suited to something, or to install.
sensesIntro.cn: fit 意为合适的、健康的、合身、适合或安装。

core.en: A match between a thing and its purpose or place.
core.cn: 事物与其用途或位置之间的契合。

branches.en: Right for a purpose.
A body in good condition.
Clothing of the right size.
A match of skills and tasks.
A part placed where it belongs.
branches.cn: 零件被安放到应在的位置。

intro.en: Fit is a short Middle English word that forms many everyday compounds.
intro.cn: fit 是中古英语的短词，构成了许多日常复合词。

latinIntro.en: Fit has no Latin ancestor; Latin aptus, fitted, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fit 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 aptus（合适的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: It was a fitting end to the day.
items.exampleCN: 这是这一天恰如其分的结尾。

items.example: The water is unfit to drink.

items.exampleCN: 她穿了一身亮眼的衣服。

definition_en: to repair something, to solve a problem, to fasten something in place, or to decide something firmly
core_image: 拧紧松动的螺丝，让摇晃的椅子重新站稳
scene: 他花了一下午修好了那把摇晃的椅子。He spent the afternoon fixing the wobbly chair.
sceneCN: 这里 fix 是「修理」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他花了一下午修好了那把摇晃的椅子。

senses.title: Repair
senses.definition: to make something whole or working again
senses.definitionCN: 使某物恢复完整或正常运转
senses.example: He fixed the wobbly chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他修好了那把摇晃的椅子。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of fixing a broken object.
senses.whyCN: 这是修理损坏物品时最日常的义项。

senses.title: Solve
senses.definition: to find a solution to a problem
senses.definitionCN: 为问题找到解决办法
senses.example: They fixed the problem in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一小时就解决了问题。
senses.why: A problem is treated like a machine that needs repair.
senses.whyCN: 问题被当作需要修理的机器来对待。

senses.title: Fasten
senses.definition: to attach something firmly in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定在某个位置
senses.example: The shelf is fixed to the wall with screws.
senses.exampleCN: 架子用螺丝固定在墙上。
senses.why: The oldest sense is driving something in until it cannot move.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是把东西钉进去使其不能移动。

senses.title: Arrange firmly
senses.definition: to decide or arrange something definitely
senses.definitionCN: 把某事明确地决定或安排好
senses.example: We fixed a date for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我们确定了会议的日期。
senses.why: Something fixed is no longer open to change.
senses.whyCN: 被固定下来的事就不再变动了。

intro.en: Fix comes from Latin figere, to fasten or drive in, through its participle fixus.
intro.cn: fix 源自拉丁语 figere（钉住、固定），经其分词 fixus 进入英语。

items.en: Figere meant to drive in or fasten.
items.cn: figere 意为钉入或固定。

items.en: The participle fixus meant fastened or fixed.

items.en: Fixare meant to fasten or settle something.

items.en: Fix named fastening and then repairing.

items.en: The word also came to mean solving or arranging.
items.cn: 这个词又引申为解决或安排。

note.en: Fix is compared with similar-looking words and with words for repair and fastening.
note.cn: 把 fix 与形近词以及表示修理和固定的词作比较。

normal.en: You fix a broken chair.

You fix a shelf to the wall.

abstract.en: To fix is to stop something from shaking.

abstract.en: A fixed point makes movement measurable.
abstract.cn: 固定的参照点让运动可以被衡量。

abstract.en: Some things are easier to fix than to explain.
abstract.cn: 有些东西修起来比解释起来容易。

examples.en: Can you fix the leaking tap?
examples.cn: 你能修一下漏水的水龙头吗？

examples.en: They fixed the date for the wedding.
examples.cn: 他们确定了婚礼的日期。

examples.en: The mirror is fixed to the wall.
examples.cn: 镜子固定在墙上。

sensesIntro.en: Fix means to repair, to solve, to fasten, or to settle something firmly.
sensesIntro.cn: fix 意为修理、解决、固定或把某事确定下来。

core.en: To make something firm and no longer loose.
core.cn: 使某物牢固、不再松动。

branches.en: A broken thing made whole again.
branches.cn: 把损坏的东西恢复完整。

branches.cn: 修理与固定共享「牢固」这一概念。

He fixated on one small detail.

latinEntries.example: The Latin verb figere meant to fasten.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语动词 figere 意为固定。

definition_zh: 闪光；一瞬间；闪现；新闻快讯

senses.title: Sudden light
senses.definition: a sudden bright burst of light
senses.definitionCN: 突然爆发的明亮光线
senses.example: The camera flash went off in the dark.

senses.title: Short moment

senses.definitionCN: 短暂地发亮或出现

senses.why: The noun became a verb of brief shining.

intro.en: Flash arose in Middle English, probably imitating a sudden splash or burst of light.

abstract.en: What arrives suddenly feels more real.

definition_zh: 平的；公寓；平淡的；瘪了的
definition_en: having an even surface, an apartment, dull without energy, or deflated
core_image: 一块刚擀开的桌面，摸不到一点起伏
scene: 我们在一间小小的公寓里住了两晚。We stayed two nights in a small flat.
sceneCN: 这里 flat 是「公寓」（第 2 个义项）；句意：我们在一间小小的公寓里住了两晚。

senses.title: Level
senses.definition: having a surface without slopes or bumps
senses.definitionCN: 表面没有倾斜或凸起的
senses.example: The land is flat for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地平坦绵延数英里。
senses.why: This is the literal physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的物理义项。

senses.title: Apartment
senses.definition: a set of rooms for living on one floor
senses.definitionCN: 位于同一层的一套住所
senses.example: We stayed two nights in a small flat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在一间小公寓里住了两晚。
senses.why: A flat is one level of a building, hence a dwelling.
senses.whyCN: 公寓占楼的一层，因此用「平」来表示。

senses.title: Dull
senses.definition: lacking interest, energy, or variation
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味、活力或变化的
senses.example: The party felt flat after the speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 讲话结束后聚会变得平淡。
senses.why: Something without peaks seems level and lifeless.
senses.whyCN: 没有起伏的东西显得平坦而无生气。

senses.title: Deflated
senses.definition: having lost air, as a tyre
senses.definitionCN: 像轮胎一样失去空气的
senses.example: The tyre went flat on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 回家路上轮胎瘪了。
senses.why: A deflated tyre is pressed flat to the ground.
senses.whyCN: 瘪胎被压平贴在地面上。

intro.en: Flat comes from Old Norse flatr, related to Old English flet, a floor or dwelling.
intro.cn: flat 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr，与古英语 flet（地板、住所）相关。

items.en: Flatr meant level or spread out.
items.cn: flatr 意为平坦的、铺开的。

items.en: Flat named a level surface.
items.cn: flat 指平坦的表面。

items.en: A flat became a dwelling on one floor.
items.cn: flat 开始指一层的住所。

items.en: The word described dull or lifeless things.
items.cn: 这个词用来形容平淡无生气的事物。

items.en: A flat tyre meant one emptied of air.
items.cn: flat tyre 指被放空空气的轮胎。

note.en: Flat is compared with similar-looking words and with words for level surfaces.
note.cn: 把 flat 与形近词以及表示平整表面的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flat is one even plane: land, a floor to live on, a mood without peaks, a tyre without air.
normalIntro.cn: flat 就是一个平面：土地、居住的一层、没有起伏的情绪、没有气的轮胎。

normal.en: The road is flat and straight.

normal.cn: 他们在城里租了一套公寓。

normal.en: The joke fell flat.
We changed the flat tyre.
Flatten the dough with a roller.

abstract.en: A flat surface hides how much ground it covers.
abstract.cn: 平坦的表面看不出它覆盖了多远。

abstract.en: Without hills, a landscape has no surprises.
abstract.cn: 没有山丘，风景就少了惊喜。

abstract.en: Even a flat road still leads somewhere.
abstract.cn: 即使平坦的路也通向某处。

examples.en: We stayed two nights in a small flat.

examples.en: The tyre went flat on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家路上轮胎瘪了。

dict_mnemonic.text: flat 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr（平坦），核心义「平」，由平的地面引申为一层公寓、平淡与瘪掉。

sensesIntro.en: Flat means level, an apartment, dull, or emptied of air.

core.en: A surface with no height or dip.

branches.en: Ground without slopes or bumps.

branches.en: A tyre pressed flat by lost air.

definition_en: the taste of food or drink, a distinctive quality, or to give food a particular taste
core_image: 一勺热汤在舌尖散开，先咸后鲜
scene: 这汤有淡淡的蒜味。The soup has a light flavour of garlic.
sceneCN: 这里 flavour 是「味道」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这汤有淡淡的蒜味。

senses.title: Taste
senses.definition: the taste that food or drink has in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 食物或饮料在口中的味道
senses.example: The soup has a light flavour of garlic.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤有淡淡的蒜味。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense used for food and drink.
senses.whyCN: 这是描述饮食时最日常的义项。

senses.title: Character
senses.definition: a distinctive quality or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 某种独特的气质或氛围
senses.example: The old town keeps a flavour of the past.
senses.exampleCN: 老城保留着过去的风味。
senses.why: Taste became a metaphor for character.
senses.whyCN: 味道被隐喻为事物的特色。

senses.title: Kind
senses.definition: a particular kind of food with a certain taste
senses.definitionCN: 带有特定味道的一类食品
senses.example: They sell ten flavours of ice cream.
senses.exampleCN: 他们卖十种口味的冰淇淋。
senses.why: Each kind of ice cream is named by its taste.
senses.whyCN: 每种冰淇淋都按味道来命名。

senses.title: To season
senses.definition: to give food a particular taste
senses.definitionCN: 给食物增添特定味道
senses.example: She flavoured the sauce with lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她用柠檬给酱汁调味。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of adding taste.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为添加味道的动词。

intro.en: Flavour comes from Old French flaor, probably from a Latin word for smell or blowing.
intro.cn: flavour 源自古法语 flaor，可能出自拉丁语中表示气味或吹拂的词。

items.en: Flare meant to blow or breathe out.
items.cn: flare 意为吹出或呼出。

items.en: Flator named a smell carried in the air.
items.cn: flator 指空气中传来的气味。

items.en: Flaor meant smell or taste.
items.cn: flaor 意为气味或味道。

items.en: Flavour named the taste of food.
items.cn: flavour 指食物的味道。

items.en: The word extended to atmosphere and character.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到氛围与特色。

note.en: Flavour is compared with similar-looking words and with words for taste and smell.
note.cn: 把 flavour 与形近词以及表示味道和气味的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flavour is what the tongue reports and what an atmosphere quietly carries.
normalIntro.cn: flavour 既是舌头报告的味道，也是氛围悄悄携带的特色。

normal.en: This tea has a floral flavour.
The town has a old flavour.
Which flavour do you want?

A flavour enhancer adds taste.

abstract.en: Taste is memory arriving through the tongue.
abstract.cn: 味道是经由舌头抵达的记忆。

abstract.en: A place has a flavour no menu can list.
abstract.cn: 一个地方的风味是菜单列不出的。

abstract.en: Small additions change the whole dish.

definition_en: the soft tissue of a body, the edible part of an animal, or the soft part of a fruit
core_image: 刀切下去，露出湿润的粉色肌理
scene: 刀切开了果肉。The knife cut through the flesh of the fruit.
sceneCN: 这里 flesh 是「果肉」（第 2 个义项）；句意：刀切开了果肉。

senses.title: Body tissue
senses.definition: the soft part of a body between skin and bone
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤与骨骼之间的柔软部分
senses.example: The wound went deep into the flesh.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口深深进了肉里。
senses.why: This is the basic anatomical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的解剖学义项。

senses.title: Fruit pulp
senses.definition: the soft edible part of a fruit
senses.definitionCN: 水果柔软可食的部分

senses.exampleCN: 刀切开了果肉。

senses.title: Physical body

senses.definitionCN: 相对于精神或心灵的肉身

senses.exampleCN: 这个故事谈论灵魂与肉体。
senses.why: Flesh came to stand for human physical nature.
senses.whyCN: flesh 进而代表人的肉体天性。

definition_en: a journey in an aircraft, the act of flying, the act of running away, or a set of stairs
core_image: 飞机抬头离地，轮子收起，地面迅速后退
scene: 我们的航班因大雪延误了。Our flight was delayed by heavy snow.

senses.title: Air journey
senses.definition: a journey made by plane
senses.definitionCN: 乘飞机进行的一次行程
senses.example: Our flight was delayed by heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的航班因大雪延误了。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.

senses.whyCN: 一段楼梯像一条连续的路程，因此同词。

intro.en: Flight comes from Old English flyht, the noun of fleogan, to fly.
intro.cn: flight 源自古英语 flyht，是 fleogan（飞）的名词形式。

items.en: The root meant to move through the air.
items.cn: 这个词根意为在空中移动。

items.en: Fleogan meant to fly.
items.cn: fleogan 意为飞。

items.en: Flyht named the act of flying.
items.cn: flyht 指飞行的行为。

items.en: Flight also meant escape from danger.
items.cn: flight 也指逃离危险。

items.en: Flight named a scheduled air journey and a run of stairs.
items.cn: flight 指定期航班和一段楼梯。

note.en: Flight is compared with similar-looking words and with words for journeys and escape.
note.cn: 把 flight 与形近词以及表示行程和逃跑的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flight is a stretch of moving through air: a plane trip, the flying itself, an escape, or a run of stairs.
normalIntro.cn: flight 是一段穿行空中的路程：航班、飞行、逃跑，或一段楼梯。

normal.en: Our flight leaves at noon.
The bird was in flight.
They took flight when the alarm rang.
The office is two flights up.
normal.cn: 办公室在上两段楼梯处。

normal.en: A flight attendant greeted us.

abstract.en: Flight is distance made by leaving the ground.
abstract.cn: 飞行是离开地面所走的距离。

abstract.en: Escape and flying share the same image.
abstract.cn: 逃跑与飞翔共享同一个意象。

abstract.en: Every stair is a small flight upward.
abstract.cn: 每一段楼梯都是一次向上的小小飞行。

examples.en: Our flight was delayed by heavy snow.
examples.cn: 我们的航班因大雪延误了。

examples.en: The flight lasted six hours.
examples.cn: 飞行持续了六个小时。

examples.en: She climbed three flights of stairs.
examples.cn: 她爬了三段楼梯。

dict_mnemonic.text: flight 是古英语 fleogan（飞）的名词，核心义「飞行的过程」，由此得到航班、逃跑与一段楼梯。

root: 源自古英语 flyht（飞行），与 fleogan（飞）同源，核心义「在空中划过的一段路」。

sensesIntro.en: Flight means an air journey, the act of flying, an escape, or a set of stairs.
sensesIntro.cn: flight 意为航班、飞行、逃跑或一段楼梯。

core.en: A continuous passage through air or upward.
core.cn: 在空中或向上的一段连续行程。

branches.en: A scheduled trip by plane.
branches.cn: 按计划乘飞机的一次行程。

branches.en: The act of moving through air.
Running away as if taking wing.
A continuous run of steps.
Flying and fleeing share one image.
branches.cn: 飞行与逃跑共享一个意象。

intro.en: Flight builds words for air travel, paths, and things that cannot fly.
intro.cn: flight 构成表示空中旅行、航线和不能飞行的词。

latinIntro.en: Flight has no Latin ancestor; Latin volatus, a flying, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flight 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 volatus（飞行）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 太空飞行始于六十年代。

items.meaning: to test an aircraft in the air
items.exampleCN: 他们对新飞机进行试飞。

definition_en: a large amount of water covering dry land, to cover an area with water, or a very large number of things
core_image: 河水漫过堤岸，把整条街变成浅海
scene: 暴雨淹没了低洼的村庄。The storm flooded the low village.
sceneCN: 这里 flood 是「淹没」（第 2 个义项）；句意：暴雨淹没了低洼的村庄。

senses.title: Overflowing water
senses.definition: a large amount of water that covers land that is usually dry
senses.definitionCN: 淹没通常干燥陆地的大量水
senses.example: The flood destroyed the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水摧毁了桥梁。
senses.why: This is the literal natural disaster.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的自然灾害。

senses.title: To cover with water
senses.definition: to cover an area with water
senses.definitionCN: 用水覆盖一片区域
senses.example: The storm flooded the low village.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨淹没了低洼的村庄。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of covering.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为覆盖的动词。

senses.title: Large amount
senses.definition: a very large number or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 数量极大的某物
senses.example: A flood of letters arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 大量信件涌来。
senses.why: Too much water became a metaphor for too much of anything.
senses.whyCN: 水太多被隐喻为任何东西太多。

senses.title: Pour in
senses.definition: to arrive or enter in very large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的数量到达或进入
senses.example: Fans flooded into the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 球迷涌入体育场。
senses.why: A crowd moving like water is said to flood in.
senses.whyCN: 像水一样移动的人群被形容为涌入。

intro.en: Flood comes from Old English flod, related to flowan, to flow.
intro.cn: flood 源自古英语 flod，与 flowan（流动）相关。

items.en: The root meant a flowing of water.
items.cn: 这个词根意为水的流动。

items.en: Flod meant a mass of moving water.
items.cn: flod 指大量流动的水。

items.en: Flood named the great water of the Bible.
items.cn: flood 指《圣经》中的大洪水。

items.en: The verb meant to cover land with water.
items.cn: 动词形式意为用水淹没土地。

items.en: The word became a metaphor for great amounts.
items.cn: 这个词成为表示大量的隐喻。

note.en: Flood is compared with similar-looking words and with words for water and abundance.
note.cn: 把 flood 与形近词以及表示水和大量的词作比较。

entries.definition: the lower surface of a room
the red liquid in the body
the rise and fall of the sea

normalIntro.en: Flood is water leaving its place and taking too much space, then any mass that behaves the same way.
normalIntro.cn: flood 是水离开原位、占据过多空间，随后任何以同样方式泛滥的东西都叫 flood。

normal.en: The river flood covered the fields.
Rain flooded the streets.
A flood of complaints followed.
People flooded into the hall.
Floodgates hold back the water.

abstract.en: Water teaches that too much of a good thing moves things away.
abstract.cn: 水告诉我们，好东西太多会把一切冲走。

abstract.en: Attention can flood as easily as a river.
abstract.cn: 注意力可以像河流一样泛滥。

abstract.en: A channel is a promise that the flood will be guided.
abstract.cn: 渠道是洪水将被引导的承诺。

examples.en: The storm flooded the low village.
examples.cn: 暴雨淹没了低洼的村庄。

examples.en: The flood destroyed the bridge.
examples.cn: 洪水摧毁了桥梁。

examples.en: A flood of letters arrived.
examples.cn: 大量信件涌来。

dict_mnemonic.text: flood 源自古英语 flod（水流），与 flow 同根，核心义「漫出原位的水」，再引申为大量与涌入。

root: 源自古英语 flod（水流、洪水），与 flow 同根，核心义「漫出边界的大量水」。

sensesIntro.en: Flood means overflowing water, to cover land with water, a huge amount, or to pour in.
sensesIntro.cn: flood 意为洪水、淹没、大量或涌入。

core.en: Water or anything else exceeding its banks.
core.cn: 水或其他东西超出边界。

branches.en: Water covering dry land.
The act of covering with water.
A huge amount of anything.
A crowd entering like water.
Water and crowds both overflow their banks.
branches.cn: 水与人群都会漫过边界。

intro.en: Flood builds words for waters, barriers, and artificial light.
intro.cn: flood 构成表示洪水、屏障和人造光的词。

latinIntro.en: Flood has no Latin ancestor; Latin inundare, to flood, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flood 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 inundare（淹没）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: the act of covering with water

definition_en: the surface of a room that you walk on, a level of a building, to surprise greatly, or to knock someone down
core_image: 光脚踩在木地板上，听见空空的回声
scene: 她坐在客厅地板上。She sat on the living-room floor.
sceneCN: 这里 floor 是「地板」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她坐在客厅地板上。

senses.title: Walking surface
senses.definition: the flat surface of a room that you walk on
senses.definitionCN: 房间里供人行走的平面
senses.example: She sat on the living-room floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在客厅地板上。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Storey
senses.definition: one level of a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑中的一层
senses.example: Her office is on the third floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她的办公室在三楼。
senses.why: Each level has its own floor surface.
senses.whyCN: 每一层都有自己的地面。

senses.title: To astonish
senses.definition: to surprise or confuse someone completely
senses.definitionCN: 使某人完全惊讶或不知所措
senses.example: The question floored me.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题把我问住了。
senses.why: Being floored is being knocked flat by surprise.
senses.whyCN: 被问倒就像被惊得趴在地上。

senses.title: To knock down
senses.definition: to hit someone so that they fall down
senses.definitionCN: 把某人打得倒下
senses.example: The punch floored him.
senses.exampleCN: 那一拳把他击倒了。
senses.why: The literal sense of sending someone to the floor.
senses.whyCN: 这是把人打到地板上的字面义。

intro.en: Floor comes from Old English flor, meaning the ground or a floor.
intro.cn: floor 源自古英语 flor，意为地面或地板。

items.en: The root named a flat ground surface.
items.cn: 这个词根指平坦的地面。

items.en: Flor meant the ground or a floor.
items.cn: flor 意为地面或地板。

items.en: Floor named the surface of a room.
items.cn: floor 指房间的地面。

items.en: Floor came to mean a level of a building.
items.cn: floor 开始指建筑的一层。

items.en: The verb meant to knock someone down.
items.cn: 动词形式意为把人击倒。

note.en: Floor is compared with similar-looking words and with words for ground and levels.
note.cn: 把 floor 与形近词以及表示地面和楼层的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Floor is the flat base of a room, one level of a building, and the ground you end on when knocked down.
normalIntro.cn: floor 是房间平坦的底面、建筑的一层，也是被击倒后落到的地方。

normal.en: The floor is cold in winter.
We live on the fourth floor.
The news floored everyone.
normal.cn: 这个消息震惊了所有人。

normal.en: He floored his opponent.
The dance floor was crowded.

abstract.en: A floor is a promise that there is a bottom.
abstract.cn: 地板是对「有底」的承诺。

abstract.en: Buildings count upward from a single surface.
abstract.cn: 建筑从一个平面开始向上计数。

abstract.en: Being floored is learning where the ground is.
abstract.cn: 被击倒就是认识地面在哪里。

examples.en: She sat on the living-room floor.
examples.cn: 她坐在客厅地板上。

examples.en: Her office is on the third floor.
examples.cn: 她的办公室在三楼。

examples.en: The punch floored him.
examples.cn: 那一拳把他击倒了。

dict_mnemonic.text: floor 源自古英语 flor（地面），核心义「脚下的平面」，由地板引申为楼层与「被打到地上」。

root: 源自古英语 flor（地面、地板），核心义「脚下平坦的底面」。

sensesIntro.en: Floor means the surface you walk on, a storey, to astonish, or to knock down.
sensesIntro.cn: floor 意为地板、楼层、使震惊或击倒。

core.en: The flat bottom surface of a space.
core.cn: 空间的平坦底面。

branches.en: The surface walked on indoors.
One level counted in a building.
Surprise that knocks you flat.
A blow that sends someone down.
The surface and the storey share one base.
branches.cn: 地板与楼层共享同一个底面。

intro.en: Floor builds words for boards, coverings, and building plans.
intro.cn: floor 构成表示地板条、铺装和建筑平面的词。

latinIntro.en: Floor has no Latin ancestor; Latin solum, ground, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: floor 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 solum（地面）只是语义对应词。

items.example: He was floored by the news.
The floorless hut was open to the ground.
items.exampleCN: 没有地板的小屋直接连着地面。
平面图显示有两间卧室。

definition_en: to move steadily like water, or a steady movement or supply of something
core_image: 河水绕过石头，连成一条不停的线
scene: 河水缓缓流过石桥。The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 flow 是「流动」（第 1 个义项）；句意：河水缓缓流过石桥。

senses.title: Move like water
senses.definition: to move steadily in a stream
senses.definitionCN: 像水流一样稳定移动
senses.example: The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 河水缓缓流过石桥。
senses.why: This is the core physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Steady movement
senses.definition: a continuous movement of people, goods, or information
senses.definitionCN: 人、货物或信息的持续移动
senses.example: The flow of traffic was heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 车流很密集。
senses.why: Water became a model for any continuous movement.
senses.whyCN: 水成为任何持续运动的模型。

senses.title: Arise from
senses.definition: to come from a source
senses.definitionCN: 从某个来源产生
senses.example: Many problems flow from poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 许多问题源于计划不周。
senses.why: A river flows from its source, and so does a result.
senses.whyCN: 河流从源头流出，结果也从原因流出。

senses.title: Supply
senses.definition: the rate at which something is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 某物被供给的速率
senses.example: They measured the flow of water.
senses.exampleCN: 他们测量了水流量。
senses.why: The movement measured over time is a flow.
senses.whyCN: 随时间计量的运动就是流量。

intro.en: Flow comes from Old English flowan, a Germanic verb for moving like water.
intro.cn: flow 源自古英语 flowan，是日耳曼语中表示像水一样移动的动词。

items.en: The root meant to flow or stream.
items.cn: 这个词根意为流动或涌流。

items.en: Flowan meant to move like water.
items.cn: flowan 意为像水一样移动。

items.en: Flow also named a rising tide.
items.cn: flow 也指上涨的潮水。

items.en: The noun named a steady movement.
items.cn: 名词形式指稳定的运动。

items.en: The word extended to traffic, money, and ideas.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到交通、金钱和思想。

note.en: Flow is compared with similar-looking words and with words for moving liquid.
note.cn: 把 flow 与形近词以及表示液体运动的词作比较。

entries.definition: to flow, as a tap does

normalIntro.en: Flow is one continuous line of movement, of water, traffic, money, or causes.
normalIntro.cn: flow 是一条连续的运动线：水、交通、金钱或原因。

normal.en: The river flows to the sea.
Traffic flows better after the fix.
Cash flow keeps a business alive.
Good results flow from good habits.
The tide ebbs and flows.

abstract.en: Water teaches that movement needs a channel.
abstract.cn: 水告诉我们运动需要通道。

abstract.en: Blocked flow builds pressure.
abstract.cn: 被阻断的流动会积聚压力。

abstract.en: Every result has a source upstream.
abstract.cn: 每个结果在上游都有源头。

examples.en: The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
examples.cn: 河水缓缓流过石桥。

examples.en: The flow of traffic was heavy.
examples.cn: 车流很密集。

examples.en: Many problems flow from poor planning.
examples.cn: 许多问题源于计划不周。

dict_mnemonic.text: flow 源自古英语 flowan（流动），与 flood、fleet 同根，核心义「像水一样连续移动」。

root: 源自古英语 flowan（流动），核心义「连续不断的移动」。

sensesIntro.en: Flow means to move like water, a steady movement, a rate of supply, or to arise from.
sensesIntro.cn: flow 意为像水一样流动、持续运动、供给流量或源自某处。

core.en: Continuous movement along a course.
core.cn: 沿通道的连续运动。

branches.en: Water moving in a stream.
Traffic or goods in motion.
A result coming from a cause.
The measured rate of supply.
Rivers and reasons both have sources.

intro.en: Flow builds words for directions, instruments, and excess.
intro.cn: flow 构成表示方向、仪器和过量的词。

latinIntro.en: Flow has no Latin ancestor; Latin fluere, to flow, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flow 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 fluere（流）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The river flowed over the bank.
The flowing water cut the stone.
The outflow of money worried them.

definition_en: the colored bloom of a plant, to produce flowers, or the finest part of something
core_image: 一朵花在清晨打开，花瓣上还挂着露水
scene: 花园里的花开了。The flowers in the garden opened.
sceneCN: 这里 flower 是「花」（第 1 个义项）；句意：花园里的花开了。

senses.title: Bloom of a plant
senses.definition: the colored part of a plant that produces seeds
senses.definitionCN: 植物产生种子的彩色部分
senses.example: The flowers in the garden opened.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里的花开了。
senses.why: This is the basic botanical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的植物学义项。

senses.title: Plant grown for blooms
senses.definition: a plant grown for its flowers
senses.definitionCN: 为观赏花而种植的植物
senses.example: She grows flowers on the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 她在阳台上种花。
senses.why: The part stands for the whole plant.
senses.whyCN: 用部分代指整株植物。

senses.title: To bloom
senses.definition: to produce flowers
senses.definitionCN: 长出花朵
senses.example: The cherry trees flower in April.
senses.exampleCN: 樱花树四月开花。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of blooming.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为开花的动词。

senses.title: Finest part
senses.definition: the best or most valuable part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物中最好或最有价值的部分
senses.example: He is in the flower of his youth.
senses.exampleCN: 他正当青春年华。
senses.why: The bloom is the peak of a plant's life.
senses.whyCN: 花是植物生命的高峰。

intro.en: Flower comes from Latin flos, flower, through Old French flour.
intro.cn: flower 经古法语 flour 上溯到拉丁语 flos（花）。

items.en: Flos meant a flower or the best part.
items.cn: flos 意为花或最好的部分。

items.en: Flour meant a flower or bloom.
items.cn: flour 意为花或花朵。

items.en: Flour named a bloom and the finest meal.
items.cn: flour 指花朵，也指最细的面粉。

items.en: Flower was respelled to show the plant sense.
items.cn: flower 被改拼以表示植物义。

items.en: Flower and flour became separate words.
items.cn: flower 与 flour 成为两个不同的词。

note.en: Flower is compared with similar-looking words and with words for blooms.
note.cn: 把 flower 与形近词以及表示花朵的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flower is the bright opening of a plant, the whole plant that bears it, and the best part of anything.
normalIntro.cn: flower 是植物明亮的绽放、承载它的整株植物，以及任何事物的精华。

normal.en: The flowers smell sweet.
She bought flowers for the table.
These trees flower in spring.
The garden is in flower.
Youth is the flower of life.

abstract.en: A flower is a plant's brief argument for beauty.
abstract.cn: 花是植物为美所作的短暂论证。

abstract.en: The best part is called the flower of the whole.
abstract.cn: 最好的部分被称为整体的花。

abstract.en: To bloom is to spend everything at once.
abstract.cn: 开花就是一次性倾尽所有。

examples.en: The flowers in the garden opened.
examples.cn: 花园里的花开了。

examples.en: The cherry trees flower in April.
examples.cn: 樱花树四月开花。

examples.en: He is in the flower of his youth.
examples.cn: 他正当青春年华。

dict_mnemonic.text: flower 与 flour 同源，均出自拉丁语 flos（花），本义「精华」，一个指花，一个指面粉。

root: 源自拉丁语 flos（花、精华），核心义「植物盛开的精华部分」。

sensesIntro.en: Flower means a plant's bloom, a flowering plant, to bloom, or the finest part.
sensesIntro.cn: flower 意为花朵、花卉、开花或精华。

core.en: The opening bloom that holds a plant's best.
core.cn: 承载植物最佳部分的绽放。

branches.en: The colored seed-bearing part.
A plant kept for its blooms.
The act of opening into bloom.
The best part of a life or thing.
branches.cn: 生命或事物最好的部分。

branches.en: The bloom is both a part and a peak.

intro.en: Flower builds words for blooms, containers, and qualities.
intro.cn: flower 构成表示花朵、容器和性质的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin flos and florem are the direct ancestors of the flower family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flos 与 florem 是 flower 词族的直接来源。

items.example: The sunflower turns to the light.

latinEntries.example: Flos is the Latin word for flower.

latinEntries.exampleCN: florem 在法语中变成 flour。
